messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — daily FinOps dashboard shows eu-west1 GPU commitment utilization dropped sharply overnight. Reserved utilization at ~42% while on-demand spend spiked.

billing-bot: :warning: Commitment-utilization alert for project:redwood-prod eu-west1 GPUs — utilization < 50% for 6 hours. Estimated wasted commit: $6.2k/day.

Ajay Patel: Wow. Any idea which routes/models are driving the on-demand spike?

Maya Chen: Quick slice from the dashboard: per-model cost shows `inference/llm-chat-16k` and `rerank-prod` had most on-demand token spend. Per-route: /chat/generic and /chat-async are highest.

Maya Chen: Posting the BigQuery snippet I used to validate (shortened):
```
SELECT route, SUM(cost) as cost, SUM(reserved_covered) as reserved
FROM `billing.gcp_export`
WHERE region = 'europe-west1' AND service = 'GPU'
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY cost DESC
```

Lena Ortiz: We had a rollout last night that pinned some Dedicated pools to us-west1 for a canary. Traffic routing fallback probably pushed a lot of EU traffic into fallback on-demand instances in eu-west1 instead of the usual reserved pool.

Tony Rivers: If that's true, commit capacity is there but misrouted. Do we have routing policy logs?

Maya Chen: I pulled routing table snapshots — the policy for `eu-prod` had a temp override to prefer region:us-west1 for a small subset, but the autoscaler didn't drain eu-west1; instead it started on-demand VMs in eu-west1 when latency SLOs dipped.

Ajay Patel: Does autoscaler create on-demand in same region by default? That could explain both wasted commit and higher cross-region egress.

Lena Ortiz: Autoscaler configured to respect region affinity but runtime fallback logic will create ondemand in region if reserved pool marked tainted/unhealthy. We saw a short health flapping in the eu-west1 reserved pool around 03:20 UTC.

Maya Chen: Daily numbers snapshot: total GPU spend yesterday = $38,400; reserved-covered = $18,100; on-demand/overage = $20,300. Estimated wasted commit (unused reserved capacity) = $6.2k/day.

finops-bot: Suggested actions: 1) Run reserved pool health sweep and force-reconcile (Tony), 2) Re-evaluate routing override from last night's rollout (Lena), 3) Short-term: temporarily shift some bursty routes to us-west1 reserved pools if possible, 4) Create a Jira to track financial impact and rollback plan.

Tony Rivers: I'll run the pool health sweep now and check node taints + GPU drivers. If it's driver flakiness we'll patch and force-rejoin.

Ajay Patel: I'll open a FinOps ticket with the spend numbers and add the per-route breakdown. Ticket will include BQ query and a couple of dashboard screenshots.

Lena Ortiz: I'll revert the rollout override and remove the routing preference to us-west1 for the affected canary.

Maya Chen: Thx — quick wins: (a) sweep and reattach reserved nodes, (b) revert override, (c) add a guard on rollout that blocks region-preference changes during peak hours.

Tony Rivers: Running sweep — ETA 18m.

Ajay Patel: Added ticket FINOPS-7834 and assigned to Maya/Tony/Lena. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FINOPS-7834

Maya Chen: Adding a note to the daily dashboard so on-call sees the commit-utilization alert in morning email.

finops-bot: Logged FINOPS-7834, snapshot attached to ticket.

Maya Chen: Closing loop — will post updates once sweep completes. :mag:

Tony Rivers: Sweep done — 3 nodes had stale driver processes, forced restart, reserved pool back to healthy. Reconciliation kicked and reserved utilization climbed to 78% within 12m.

Maya Chen: Nice — cost projection shows saving ~ $5.8k/day if we keep routing steady. Leaving ticket open for postmortem and gating deploy change. :+1:
